property_summary: For any admissible input that does not revert, the reference C returns true, but the mutant returns false, violating the invariant that a successful transfer call always returns true.
For any input that does not revert, a successful call to transfer returns the value from the boolean cast of the external call result, not a hardcoded constant.
For any input that does not revert, the reference always returns true, but the mutant returns false, so the return value must equal true.

For any admissible input that does not revert, transfer returns the same value as the success of the last low-level call (true if the call succeeded, false if it failed), but the mutant always returns false.

For any set of transfer amounts where each v[i] is zero or does not overflow when multiplied by the decimal multiplier, reference C always sends v[i]*10^18 tokens; mutant M sends only v[i] tokens, so whenever at least one v[i] > 0, the transferred amounts differ.

The reference C ensures that when msg.sender is the required address and each v[i] passes the zero or safe-multiplication check, the low-level call to caddress always includes the same calldata as the mutant except the mutant uses v[i]*1 instead of v[i]*10^18, causing a difference in the success return value of the transfer call itself if the external call's return value is checked and differs.

For any valid input, the reference C's transfer returns true; the mutant M's transfer returns true as well, but the actual low-level call payload differs in the amount argument, causing a divergence in the observed behavior of the specified caddress contract.

For any admissible input, the correct contract always sends tokens with the 10^18 multiplier and succeeds externally, while the mutant sends tokens without the multiplier, causing the external call to revert when the receiver rejects a smaller-than-expected amount.

For any input where the external call succeeds in both P and M, the return value of P.transfer (true) must equal that of M.transfer (true), but the bug can cause M to revert when the external call fails due to insufficient tokens approved/available, making the return value differ (revert vs true).

For any admissible input where a v[i] value causes multiplication overflow such that (v[i] * 1e18) / v[i] != 1e18, the reference contract reverts the entire transaction while the mutant proceeds with the call to caddress.

For any call to transfer with arrays where at least one v[i] > 0, the reference contract ensures the external call is made with a scaled amount; the mutant incorrectly makes the call with any v[i] value, causing the scaling to differ when v[i] does not satisfy the multiplication overflow check.

For any call to transfer where all v[i] avoid arithmetic overflow on the multiplication, the reference always performs the external call with the correctly scaled amount (v[i]*1e18), while the mutant performs it with the same scaled amount only if the require is satisfied; the mutant will instead proceed with a corrupted encoding when an overflow occurs because the scaling expression is evaluated unconditionally, but the reference reverts, so after transfer returns the state of caddress’s contract (specifically the transfer result observed via return data) is identical for all admissible inputs—this is trivially true and thus broken.

For any call to transfer where the external low-level call to caddress succeeds in both versions (i.e., caddress has code that does not revert on arbitrary calldata), the return value of transfer (true) is identical; however, the mutant always executes the external call regardless of the overflow check, so when caddress is an adversarial contract that reverts on the malformed calldata produced by the mutant's overflowed scaling, the reference's revert on the failed require prevents the external call entirely while the mutant's call reverts, causing the overall transaction outcome to differ.

For any call to transfer where at least one v[i] overflows when multiplied by 1e18, the reference reverts due to the require guard and does not call caddress, while the mutant always calls caddress, so if caddress is an adversarial contract that consumes all gas on the corrupt calldata, the gas used in the reference transaction differs from the mutant's (the mutant consumes more gas up to call failure).

For any valid transfer call, the reference contract always succeeds without reverting unless it attempts to transfer 0 tokens to any recipient, which may cause a downstream revert; the buggy contract reverts for inputs where the unscaled v[i] would overflow during multiplication.
